item.title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of Muscina stabulans Fallén (Diptera: Muscidae)
item.description:
Yingna Zhang, Liangliang Li, Jianfeng Jin, Jiangtao Mei, Ruixin Zhu, Yu Wang
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08509-0
Abstract Muscina stabulans (Diptera: Muscidae) exhibits a saprophagous–predatory dual-niche life history and is widely used as a forensic indicator. However, the lack of a high-quality reference genome has limited phylogenomics, functional genomics, and the genomic interpretation of forensic traits in this lineage. Here, we present the first chromosome-level reference genome for M. stabulans , generated by integrating PacBio HiFi long reads, Illumina short reads, and Hi-C data. The assembly spans 747.50 Mb (scaffold N50 = 136.70 Mb), with 98.99% of the assembled sequence (739.97 Mb) anchored into five pseudochromosomes. BUSCO analysis (n = 1,367) indicates 97.8% completeness (96.3% single-copy and 1.5% duplicated BUSCOs). High assembly quality is supported by high read-mapping rates, per-pseudochromosome BUSCO completeness, a high LTR Assembly Index (19.86), concordant chromosome-scale coverage, terminal telomeric repeats, and GC content consistency with other muscid genomes. Repetitive elements account for 61.33% of the genome, and we annotated 12,693 protein-coding genes. This chromosome-level genome provides a robust foundation for Muscina spp. genomics and comparative studies across Muscidae.

item.title: A strongly annotated passive acoustic dataset for tropical bird monitoring
item.description:
Daniela Ruiz, Juan Sebastián Ulloa, Zhongqi Miao, Nicolás Betancourt, Maria Paula Toro-Gómez, Andrés Hernández, Bruno Demuro, Eliana Barona-Cortés, et al.
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08574-5
Abstract Passive acoustic monitoring enables continuous, non-invasive biodiversity assessment across diverse ecosystems. The scale of these datasets has driven the adoption of machine learning, with supervised approaches showing strong performance. However, supervised methods require time-resolved annotated datasets, which remain scarce, especially in complex tropical soundscapes. We present PteroSet, a curated dataset of strongly annotated Neotropical bird vocalizations recorded in Puerto Asís (Putumayo) and Pivijay (Magdalena), Colombia, between 2023 and 2025. The dataset comprises 563 recordings (73.62 h) and 15,372 time–frequency annotations, including 6,702 events identified to the species level across 168 species. We release the annotations in a COCO-inspired JSON schema that unifies audio files, taxonomic categories, and labels for machine learning workflows. Beyond providing annotated data, PteroSet serves as a realistic benchmark that highlights key characteristics of tropical soundscapes, including acoustic co-occurrence and domain shift across recording sites. We provide a deep learning baseline for binary bird detection, demonstrating PteroSet’s usability and the challenges it presents.

item.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the black-spotted frog (Pelophylax nigromaculatus)
item.description:
Gang Wan, Wentao Cao, Xiaoqing Wang, Jianguo Xiang, Dongwu Wang, Ming Yang, Rongquan Zheng, Yazhou Hu
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08542-z
Abstract Pelophylax nigromaculatus is an East Asian ranid frog that is commercially cultured in China. We generated a chromosome-level reference assembly using PacBio HiFi, short-read, and Hi-C data. The assembly contains 5.06 Gb of non-gap sequence, of which 4.88 Gb (96.48%) was anchored to 13 chromosome-scale scaffolds. The contig N50 and scaffold N50 are 31.64 Mb and 576.86 Mb, respectively. Genome-mode BUSCO recovered 95.26% of 3,354 vertebrate orthologues. Repetitive sequences span 3.93 Gb (77.61%), and the annotation contains 32,557 protein-coding genes, 31,715 of which have functional assignments. Terminal TTAGGG/CCCTAA arrays were detected at 17 of 26 chromosome ends. The assembly, annotation, and raw sequencing data are publicly available as a chromosome-level genomic resource for P. nigromaculatus .

item.title: The first chromosomal-level genome assembly of Stingless bee Lepidotrigona flavibasis Cockerell, 1929 (Hymenoptera, Apidae, Meliponini)
item.description:
Dahe Yang, Junpeng Ma, Changsheng Ma, Hua Wang, Kunlin Wan, Xinmeng Li, Tianzheng Xu, Yaoting Zhang, et al.
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08126-x
Abstract This is the first genome assembly of a yellow striped stingless bee species Lepidotrigona flavibasis at the chromosomal level. Specimens were collected from Yunnan Province, China, and sequenced using PacBio HiFi long-read (Sequel II), RNA-seq (transcriptome), and Hi-C technologies. The assembly was generated via de novo assembly with HiFiasm, scaffolded to chromosomes using YaHS with Hi-C data, and manually curated in Juicebox. The final 251.74 Mb assembly comprises 16 chromosomes (Contig N50 = 10.74 Mb), exhibiting high continuity and accuracy (94.6% BUSCO completeness). Hi-C interaction maps confirmed distinct chromosomal compartmentalization. The genome contained a total of 42.13 Mb of repetitive sequences, accounting for 14.90% of the entire genome. A total of 10,041 genes were annotated across the whole genome using transcriptomic (RNA-seq) evidence, among which 8, 972 genes were successfully functionally annotated from various databases. The first high-quality reference genome of Lepidotrigona constructed in this study provides a fundamental resource for the evolutionary, ecological and conservation genomics research of stingerless bees.
